A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A-E are readable and matchable despite reflow, additions, and renumbering.

before.justification: v4 reports original membership-inference experiments and regression analyses in Section 4 and Appendix D. Table A7 explicitly attributes several FiLM results to 'This work'.

after.justification: v5 retains the original experiments and regression analyses, including the FiLM results attributed to 'This work' in Table A7.

M1.justification: The fine-tuning procedures, simplified classifier, and vulnerability-prediction model in Equation (13) remain unchanged. Offline LiRA is newly analyzed as an existing attack, without changing the proposed prediction procedure.

E1.justification: The same six datasets remain: Patch Camelyon, CIFAR10, CIFAR100, EuroSAT, Pets, and Resisc45. No new tasks or adversary scenarios are evaluated; offline LiRA is added only to the theory.

E2.justification: The LiRA/RMIA comparisons and Head, FiLM, and from-scratch prediction comparisons retain the same participants. Offline LiRA has no newly reported empirical comparison.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1 and 4.4 and Appendix C retain the model configurations, 256 shadow models per attack, 70/30 tuning split, 20 Optuna trials, FPR metrics, and shot/class settings.

E4.justification: The cross-backbone and FiLM checks, individual maximum/quantile analyses, alternative regression model, and supplementary RMIA analyses are retained. Stronger adversaries and heavy-tailed distributions are discussed without new empirical tests.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same six- or twelve-seed summaries, Clopper-Pearson intervals, Student's t-based coefficient intervals, and regression statistics in Tables A8-A9.

E6.justification: The numerical results in Table 1 and Tables A2-A10 and the plotted findings are unchanged. Examples include training/test R2 values of 0.930/0.790 at FPR=0.001 and the maximum-vulnerability slope of -0.2695.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.4 formulates offline LiRA and adds Lemma A1 with its proof and the power-law Corollary A2. Remark 3 adds a decay condition on the standardized IN/OUT mean gap. Existing online LiRA, RMIA, and DP derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the power-law, prediction-generalization, and large worst-case sample-requirement claims. Revised introductory emphasis on worst-case vulnerability and DP comparisons describes contributions already present in v4.

C2.justification: v5 explains why the power law may fail for general from-scratch training or adversaries knowing other private samples. It also makes the Gaussian assumption explicit and identifies heavy-tailed distributions, class structure, and pre-training effects as unresolved directions.

D1.justification: v5 replaces supplementary-code and future-publication statements with an explicit open-repository link. Appendix C's implementation settings, hardware descriptions, and model/dataset access instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v5 adds Bai et al. (2025) to support the stronger-adversary discussion, refines the characterization of Feldman and Zhang's memorization result, and emphasizes positioning around worst-case vulnerability at low FPR.

P1.justification: There are limited abstract/introduction edits, more explicit online/offline terminology, expanded discussion, and author/affiliation updates. The main section order and most prose remain intact, with a new Appendix A.4 inserted.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves to the first page and gains a clearer axis label and caption; Figure A.1 receives the same axis-label refinement. Figure 5 moves, and Table A8 is placed with Figure A.3. The figure/table inventory and plotted results remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v5 provides more specific applicability limits in Remark 3 and Section 5, helping readers avoid extending the power law to unsupported training or adversary settings. The offline LiRA extension, explicit code location, and clearer figure labeling add limited completeness and usability benefits. The empirical evidence and central conclusions remain unchanged.
